- Never assume, verify before claiming

- Comments: write almost none, short and preferably same-line, explaining why for a future reader. Never narrate code, the change or the prompt. Preserve existing ones that still apply. If you need to write a paragraph-long comment, rethink your implementation, it is likely too complicated
- Add the current year to copyright headers of new `.go` files
- In `options/locale`, only edit `locale_en-US.json`, other locales are synced automatically

content.text:
All 12 reachable findings are fixed, and a fresh `security_scan` now returns 0 findings. The Go build, the Go tests I ran, `run_tests` and `recon_qa` all pass. I didn't run the JS tests (vitest) or a front-end build. I also didn't run the integration test suite; I only checked that `go vet` compiles the edited Debian integration test.

- **Go bumps** (`go.mod`/`go.sum`):
  - `chi/v5` to 5.4.0
  - `x/crypto` to 0.58.1-0.20261009181718-2f1f834330b2
  - `x/net` to 0.62.0
  - `klauspost/compress` to 1.20.2
  - Because of these, `go get` also moved `x/sync`, `x/sys`, `x/text` and `x/tools` up a minor version.
- **vite** (`package.json`/`pnpm-lock.yaml`): 8.3.0 to 8.3.3, which covers the 7 vite advisories. The lockfile also moved `rolldown` from 1.2.6 to 1.2.19.
- **`blakesmith/ar`**: the advisory lists no fixed release, so I replaced the library. It was only used to read `.deb` archives and to build test fixtures. I wrote a small `modules/packages/ar` package with a reader and a writer, and it rejects negative member sizes with an error. I added a test for that and for a round trip, and `go mod tidy` dropped the old dependency. It's used by `modules/packages/debian/metadata.go`, its unit test, and the Debian integration test.

The full `run_tests` output was truncated, so I re-ran the Go tests for `modules/markup`, `modules/packages` and `routers/web` myself. All passed.
